perientia frequens fieri docet ) quam propensi sint
Homines, ac veluti parati ad incidendum in has
fraudes; adeo ut etiam contra sanæ Rationis Dic-
ta, malint probabilibus Argumentis, & suo Arbitrio
permissis, utrum admittantur, vel non, persuaderi,
quam irrefragabilibus ad Assensum cogi. Valida
Argumentorum Tela, quasi tot Hostium infensorum
Arma, refo[?] midare[?] solemus, & a nobis repellere; at
speciosas verorum Hostium fallacias sponte admitti-
mus, & sub Colloquii obtentu in Insidias cadimus.
Sic Aviculæ incidunt in Retia dolosa, dum Aucu-
pis fistulæ incautius auscultant. Sic molles lenesque
adblandientis solis Radii, viatorem illum paulatim
denudant, quem ventus asperrimus atque validissi-
mus, omni vi sua, vestibus spoliare non potuit. Sic
Retiarius Myrmillonem vincit, ducitque captivum.
Sic demum, hostis infensissimus humani Generis,
sagis & veneficis obsequium suum promptissime exhi-
bere videtur, dum ad eorum nutum simul appareet, et
voluntati paret, adque illorum arbitrium se in spe-
ciem accommodat, cum interim iisdem revera impe-
ret, eosque suæ Potestati subditos habeat. Iftiusmo-
di artificia Socinus hic usu pavit, qui contradicen-
tes patientissime ferre solitus est, & placidissime
tractare, donec hoc tandem effecerit, ut speciosa
Humilitatis ac modestiæ ostentatione, cum emen-
tito veritatis tuendæ atque propagandæ studio con-
juncta, Adversarium in suas partes pertraxerit, at-
que hoc sæpenumero effecit, non tam speciosis Ra-
tionum momentis, quam simulatione modestiæ. Ex-
emplo sit illud Socini Responsum, quo afferuit, nul-
lam esse necessitatem ordinationis in Ecclesia, quæ

page.notes: The running head reads "De fana, sive recta Ratione." in the scan; the long s makes "sana" likely, so I read it as sana with the first letter uncertain. "refo midare" in the line "Valida Argumentorum Tela" is badly blurred and was marked [?]. The text was set as one continuous paragraph on this page, since no line is indented. The catchword "à" is at the lower right. The lower part of the page is clear enough to read, though the print is faint in places, especially "apparet", "usu", and "ostentatione", which are not marked because the letters are readable.
